reason: The bone framework has spaces awaiting mineral, and the goal is to strengthen it.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the bone framework.

alternatives.reason: Building a muscle is another stated goal, but the mineral fitting is clear too.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bones while the elbow stayed movable; the muscles still need to be built and attached.
reaction: It was useful to see that the joint tissues stayed unmineralized.
reason: The goal says to build the muscles from cells and supporting tissue, so I'll start with the front group.
expectation: The cells and supporting tissue should form the front muscle.

alternatives.reason: I could build the back muscle first instead.

effect: The front cells and supporting tissue formed the biceps, with tendon ends that can connect it to bones.
reaction: Seeing the separate cells become long fibres helped me picture the muscle.
reason: The back muscle also needs to be built from its cells and supporting tissue.
expectation: They should form the back upper-arm muscle with tendon ends.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the front muscle first, but I'll build the back one now.

effect: Both muscles are built; they now need to be attached on opposite sides of the elbow.
reaction: The picture made the back muscle's attachment clearer.
reason: The biceps belongs at the front of the arm, so I'll attach it to the movable skeleton.
expectation: The biceps should attach across the front of the elbow.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the back muscle first instead.

effect: The biceps is attached across the front of the elbow and can pull the forearm to bend it; the triceps still needs attaching.
reaction: The arrows helped me picture how the pull bends the elbow.
reason: The triceps belongs on the back, opposite the attached biceps.
expectation: The triceps should attach across the back of the elbow.

effect: The completed arm shows how the two muscles pull from opposite sides to bend and straighten the elbow. All chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The two views made the opposing pulls easy to picture.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the triceps was most worthwhile because the two views showed how both muscles work together to move the elbow in opposite directions.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the back muscle repeated much of the front muscle construction, though the comparison helped show their different positions.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the supporting tissue to continue into the tendon ends that attach muscle to bone.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the goals and pictures made the pairings clear.

continue.text: Yes. Seeing familiar arm movement explained through the parts was satisfying, and I'd be curious to see another body system built the same way.
